title: chore(mcp): reword the registry description; allow metadata-only republish
body:
Registry listing becomes:

> **Actenon Kernel**
> Verify consequential AI actions before they execute.

(The title was already `Actenon Kernel`; only the description changes. 52 chars, under the schema's 100 limit — validated against the official `2025-12-11` schema.)

## Why this needed a workflow change

Registry metadata is **immutable per server version** — the [FAQ](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry) is explicit: *"Submit a new server.json with a unique version string. Once published, version metadata is immutable."* So rewording a description requires a new **server** version.

It does not require new **code**. The registry deliberately models `version` (the server listing) and `packages[].version` (the artifact) as separate fields, so this ships as server `1.2.2` pointing at the already-published package `1.2.1`. The alternative — cutting an identical PyPI 1.2.2 to carry a blurb — would put permanent noise in the release history for nothing.

My original gate forced all three versions into lockstep, which would have blocked this. Relaxed to preserve the guarantee that actually matters:

- `verify-claims` fails if `packages[].version` is **ahead** of `pyproject` (a listing pointing at an unreleased package), or if the server version is **behind** the package it ships. Drift in the safe direction is allowed.
- `publish-mcp-registry` keeps **full lockstep on tag releases** — a real release must still ship its own package — and relaxes only for `workflow_dispatch`.
- The PyPI wait step now polls the version **the listing declares** rather than pyproject's, which is the version the registry actually validates.

Verified locally in both modes: dispatch-mode precheck passes, `packages[].version` 1.2.1 resolves on PyPI (HTTP 200), and the coherence check reports `server 1.2.2, package 1.2.1, pyproject 1.2.1`.

After merge I'll run `publish-mcp-registry` via `workflow_dispatch` and confirm the new description in the live registry API.

title: fix: MCP Registry namespace case + never-run sigstore signing
body:
Two release-path defects, both first observable on the v1.2.0 tag.

## 1. Registry namespace is case-sensitive

The v1.2.0 registry publish failed with a 403 that names the problem exactly:

> You have permission to publish: `io.github.Actenon/*`. Attempting to publish: `io.github.actenon/kernel`.

I lowercased the org name. Corrected to `io.github.Actenon/kernel`.

This costs a version rather than an amendment: the registry proves PyPI ownership via an `mcp-name:` marker in the README, and PyPI freezes that README into the immutable package description. So the fix ships as **1.2.1** — forward, never a re-cut of 1.2.0.

`verify-claims.yml` now derives the expected namespace from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` and fails pre-merge, so this class of error costs a CI run instead of a published version.

## 2. The sigstore signing job has never run

`supply-chain.yml`'s `sigstore-release` job is gated on `refs/tags/v*`. It reported "skipping" on every PR and had never actually executed — v1.2.0 was its first real run, and it failed:

```
sigstore: error: Error: --signature and --certificate must be used together.
```

`--output-certificate` requires `--output-signature` alongside it. The job now emits only `--bundle`, which already contains the certificate and the signature.

## Verified

PyPI 1.2.0 itself is sound — I pulled the published wheel and confirmed `actenon-mcp = actenon.mcp_server:main` is registered and `actenon/mcp_server.py` is bundled. (An earlier `uvx` check appeared to fail only because PyPI's simple index lagged the JSON API and resolved 1.1.0.)

title: feat(mcp): ship a connectable MCP server with zero-install demo mode
body:
WO-18. The MCP adapter already worked — `actenon/adapters/mcp.py` is **untouched** by this PR. What was missing was any way for a stranger to *use* it: no runnable binary, no registry listing, no config block to paste.

## Connect in sixty seconds

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "actenon": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "actenon-kernel[mcp]", "actenon-mcp", "--demo"]
    }
  }
}
```

## The tools

| Tool | Answers | Side effects |
|---|---|---|
| `actenon_verify` | Would this proof be accepted for this exact action? | None — consumes no replay state, emits no receipt |
| `actenon_gate` | ALLOW or a typed refusal | Enforcement: consumes single-use replay state, emits a hash-chained Receipt/Refusal |
| `actenon_receipt` | What happened, and was the log rewritten? | None — returns the artifact plus chain position and hashes |

Every response carries **both** the machine `reason_code` and the human-readable reason. That is the point of shipping this as a server: the model can see *why* it was refused.

## Demo mode is unmistakably demo mode

`--demo` uses an ephemeral per-process key and in-memory state — no configuration read, no network call, no key on disk. Every tool description is prefixed `DEMO MODE — ephemeral key, not for production.`, three startup lines say so on stderr, and demo mode is **refused outright** in a production-like environment.

`actenon_demo_grant` exists **only** in demo mode and is absent from a non-demo server. In a real deployment the grant comes from `actenon-permit` after human approval — a verifier that issues its own authority is not a verifier. This is a deliberate addition to the three tools the work order specified; flagging it explicitly.

## Fail-closed without `--demo` (WO-8)

Missing `--key-file`, a nonexistent path, and an empty key file each exit non-zero with a message naming the demo alternative. Key material is read from a path and never logged.

## Registry

`server.json` (validated against the official `2025-12-11` schema) plus `publish-mcp-registry.yml`, which publishes to the official MCP Registry from CI using **GitHub OIDC** — no stored token, no interactive login. `verify-claims.yml` now machine-checks the registry ownership marker and that `server.json`, `pyproject.toml`, and the git tag agree, so the listing cannot silently rot.

Note: `modelcontextprotocol/servers` no longer accepts community listings (verified — it is reference implementations only, and directs community servers to the registry).

## Verified

- Live stdio client handshake via `uvx` from a clean `HOME` — tool list and smoke call in `MCP_QUICKSTART.md`
- The scripted conversation is **generated output**, not an illustration: refuse → grant → attempt to widen → `ACTION_MISMATCH` → retry in scope → ALLOW → replay → `DUPLICATE_REPLAY` → fetch receipt
- `pytest tests/ -q`: 632 passed, 3 skipped (20 new tests, incl. a socket-blocking test proving demo mode opens no network connection)
- `pytest tests/integration/ -k mcp -q`: 29 passed, 2 skipped
- ruff check + format clean

title: fix: settle SQLite state before bundle export hashing; incident simulate printer KeyError
body:
## What

Fixes the flaky `test_bundle_verify_reports_success_for_exported_bundle` (failed on main run [30118860793](https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-kernel/actions/runs/30118860793) before either open PR existed, and again on #21/#22 including a rerun) plus a deterministic CLI bug found while diagnosing it.

## Root causes

**1. Bundle export hash race (the flake).** `bundle export` hashes `*.sqlite3` files, then zips them. A replay-store connection left to garbage collection checkpoints its WAL into the main database file whenever CPython finalizes it — including *between* the hash pass and the archive write. Verify then reports `File hash mismatch: labs/local_proof/state/replay.sqlite3`. This is the same failure class as the existing WAL/SHM hashing exclusion, one layer deeper. Export now runs `gc.collect()` plus `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` on every database file before hashing.

**2. Incident simulate printer (deterministic, masked).** `simulate --incident <name>` **without** `--json` always exited 1 with `ERROR: 'refusal_code'` — the human-readable printer indexes keys that incident results don't carry. Every passing test uses `--json`; the flaky test ignored the simulate exit code, so this never surfaced. The printer now uses `.get()`.

## Verification

- 40 consecutive up → simulate → export → verify cycles clean on Python 3.12 (previously failed within 6 iterations, error captured from the JSON payload)
- `pytest tests/` on 3.12: 611 passed, 4 skipped
- Non-JSON incident simulate now exits 0

title: ci: three-way version coherence gate (pyproject / tag / PyPI)
body:
## What

Replaces the one-directional version-drift gate (WO-19 4.5) with a three-way coherence gate: `scripts/check_version_coherence.py` + `.github/workflows/version-coherence.yml` (PRs, pushes to main, and a **daily schedule** — a publish can fail silently after a tag is pushed, and no PR will exist to catch it). The old `version-drift.yml` is removed so exactly one version check remains.

## Assertions

| | scope | on failure |
|---|---|---|
| **A** `pyproject >= PyPI latest` | PRs + main | hard fail — the rollback check; message states the rule: *never lower a version to pass a check — bump forward instead* |
| **B** `newest release tag == PyPI latest` | main + daily | hard fail — everything tagged gets published, nothing published is untagged (the WO-19 defect class) |
| **C** `pyproject == newest tag` | main + daily | warn — legitimate mid-release state; escalates to hard fail once the bump commit is older than 7 days |

Comparisons use `packaging.version.Version`. Release tags are selected by pattern (`v<maj>.<min>.<patch>`) across all tags rather than git topology — this org carries foreign-namespace tags (`ts-sdk-v*`, `ts-types-v*`, `v1`, `*-integration`) and at least one release tag that is not an ancestor of main after a history rewrite. Repos with no tags or no PyPI release are treated as 0.0.0 with the relevant assertion skipped and noted.

## Why the old gate was insufficient

It only asked "does a tag exist for the pyproject version?" — a rollback trivially satisfies that (the *old* tag exists), which is exactly how the actenon-protocol 1.2.0 → 1.1.0 rollback passed. Both failure directions were demonstrated against the new gate before shipping (ASSERT A on a deliberately lowered version, ASSERT B on a deliberately unpublished tag).

title: feat: base install verifies Ed25519 — cryptography moved to runtime dependencies
body:
## What

Moves `cryptography>=42` from the `[asymmetric]` extra into `[project].dependencies`, and bumps the kernel to **1.1.0**.

## Why

The reference broker (`actenon-permit`) declares `actenon-kernel[asymmetric]` and mints **Ed25519** proofs in production. A third party running `pip install actenon-kernel` got a verifier that could not verify the artifacts this ecosystem actually produces — 15 of 33 conformance tests skipped. The ecosystem's core claim is that *any party can verify without trusting Actenon*; that fails if the default install cannot verify the real thing.

The 1.0.0-run FINDINGS.md defended the base install by noting the HMAC path (`build_local_proof_signer()`) runs fully — but that same run demoted `build_local_proof_signer()` to development-only. The base install was justified by the path simultaneously labelled unfit for production. That conclusion is reversed here; a follow-up docs PR appends the resolution block to FINDINGS.md.

## Compatibility

Additive under the published compatibility promise: no API change, nothing that previously verified stops verifying. The `[asymmetric]` extra is **retained** (it now restates the base dependency) so existing `actenon-kernel[asymmetric]` specs keep resolving.

## Verified locally

- Clean venv, `pip install .` with **no extras**: `cryptography 49.0.0` present, **33/33 conformance tests execute and pass, zero skips**
- Fresh Ed25519 counter-signature minted and verified end to end on the base install (tamper control rejected)
- `scripts/assert_dep_direction.py`: `OK: kernel runtime actenon deps = ['actenon-protocol']`
- Clean-install closure: exactly 2 actenon packages (kernel + protocol)
- `pytest tests/ -q`: 611 passed, 4 skipped (non-crypto optional deps)

## CI changes

`invariants.yml` base-install job now asserts cryptography **is** present and hard-fails on any skipped conformance test (it previously asserted the opposite and merely reported the skip count).

After merge: tag `v1.1.0` → publish workflow → PyPI.

title: Add SBOM + pip-audit + sigstore scaffolding (Fable 5 Part 3G)
body:
Brings the kernel's supply chain to parity with cloud and makes it the strictest in the ecosystem.

New workflow `.github/workflows/supply-chain.yml` runs on every push, PR, and release tag with three jobs:

- **sbom**: CycloneDX SBOM generation; uploaded as artefact; build provenance attested on tags.
- **pip-audit**: OSV vulnerability database audit; fails build on any known vuln; SARIF to GitHub Security tab.
- **sigstore-release**: on release tags, keyless Sigstore signing of wheel + sdist (OIDC-bound); anyone can verify a published wheel was built by this workflow.

`SECURITY.md` documents the supply chain posture and what is on the roadmap (reproducible builds, SLSA L3, hash-pinned deps).

Refs: Fable 5 Part 3G.

title: Add concrete AWS KMS signer + key-lifecycle state machine (Fable 5 Part 3C)
body:
Closes Fable 5 Part 3C: the universal gate across every persona.

## What

First concrete KMS backend in the tree. Adds:

- `actenon/proof/signers/key_lifecycle.py` — five-state machine (active, retired, suspended, revoked, hard_revoked). Only `active` can sign. Everything except `hard_revoked` can verify.
- `actenon/proof/signers/aws_kms.py` — concrete AWS KMS backend implementing `ExternalManagedSigningBackend`. Boto3 is lazy/optional. Maps AWS KeyState to Actenon lifecycle. More restrictive state wins on disagreement.
- `tests/unit/test_aws_kms_signer.py` — 41 new tests (lifecycle, backend, rotation scenario).
- `docs/reference/ecosystem/KMS_ROTATION_RUNBOOK.md` — operator runbook (executed procedure, not described).
- `pyproject.toml` — `[aws]` optional extra.

## Verification

- 602 kernel tests pass (was 561; +41).
- Tests use mock KMS client — no real AWS calls.
- `make verify-claims` passes.

## What this does NOT do

- Does not provision KMS keys (operator via Terraform/CFN).
- Does not auto-rotate (per runbook, rotation is an operator action).
- Does not implement GCP/Azure/HSM (AWS is first; others are follow-ups).
- Does not bill anything.

The lifecycle state machine is provider-neutral; future backends reuse it.

Refs: Fable 5 Part 3C.

title: Replay, idempotency, key lifecycle, and adversarial hardening (Phase 6)
body:
## Summary

Formalises the replay vs idempotency model, fixes audit K-04 (the 2 pre-existing test failures), and adds the 8-state outcome reconciliation model.

## Replay model

**Replay protection** prevents unauthorised reuse of proof authority. Keyed by `proof_id` (pccb_id). A consumed proof is rejected as `DUPLICATE_REPLAY`. This is enforced by the `ReplayStore.claim_once()` / `mark_consumed()` / `release_claim()` cycle in the `ProtectedExecutor`.

Replay state is claimed AFTER all non-mutating verification passes (steps 1–13 of the Phase 4 pipeline). This ensures replay state is never consumed for an invalid proof.

## Idempotency model

**Idempotency** allows safe recovery or retry of an intended operation without duplicating its side effect. Keyed by `operation_id` + `action_hash`. The `IdempotencyStore` is checked BEFORE the replay claim:

| Scenario | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Same `operation_id` + same `action_hash` (new proof) | Return prior result (idempotent replay) |
| Same `operation_id` + different `action_hash` | Refuse with `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` |
| Different `operation_id` | Normal execution |

An idempotency key is NOT permission to reuse a proof indefinitely. The proof must still pass replay protection (single-use). Idempotency only applies when a NEW proof is minted for the SAME operation.

Identifier model: `proof_id` (replay), `operation_id` (idempotency), `attempt_id`/`request_id` (receipt linkage), `reconciliation_state` (8-state outcome).

## Key lifecycle rules

The kernel's key lifecycle is enforced by the `PCCBVerifier` (Phase 4):
- **Algorithm allow-listing**: the signer validates the signature algorithm. Only `EdDSA` and `HS256` (dev-only) are accepted.
- **Key rotation**: via `verify_with_metadata` which resolves the issuer's key at verification time.
- **Expired keys**: the time-validity check (step 6) rejects proofs past `expires_at`.
- **Revoked keys**: the `revocation_checker` callable (step 13) rejects proofs whose authority has been revoked.
- **Unknown keys**: the signer rejects signatures from unknown key IDs.
- **SSRF resistance**: key discovery is delegated to the signer (well-known URL resolver with SSRF protection).
- **Fail-closed**: if the revocation checker errors, the proof is refused.

## DoS protections

Already enforced by the Phase 4 verifier:
- **Proof size**: 1 MiB max canonical output (via `canonicalize_bytes`).
- **Nesting depth**: 32 max depth (via `_validate_depth`).
- **String lengths**: enforced by the 1 MiB output limit.
- **Verification timeouts**: the verifier is synchronous; timeouts are the caller's responsibility.

## Outcome-state model (8 states)

| State | Description |
|---|---|
| `REFUSED_BEFORE_EXECUTION` | Proof was refused; no execution attempted |
| `VERIFIED_NOT_EXECUTED` | Proof verified but execution not attempted (policy denial) |
| `EXECUTION_ATTEMPTED` | Handler was called but result not yet known |
| `PROVIDER_CONFIRMED_SUCCESS` | Handler returned; provider confirmed success |
| `PROVIDER_CONFIRMED_FAILURE` | Handler returned; provider confirmed failure |
| `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` | Handler raised; provider may have accepted. Reconciliation required. |
| `RECONCILED_SUCCESS` | Reconciler determined action completed successfully |
| `RECONCILED_FAILURE` | Reconciler determined action did not complete |

## Vulnerabilities fixed

| Vulnerability | Fix |
|---|---|
| Audit K-04: replay vs idempotency conflated | IdempotencyStore returns prior result for same operation_id + same action_hash instead of DUPLICATE_REPLAY |
| Audit K-04: no conflict detection for same operation_id + different action_hash | IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT refusal code |
| No outcome-state model for ambiguous provider outcomes | 8-state OutcomeState enum with is_terminal / is_reconcilable |

## Residual risks

- The `IdempotencyStore` is in-memory. Production deployments need a persistent store (SQLite/Postgres).
- The reconciliation interface (`actenon.reconciliation`) is reserved but not yet wired to the executor's outcome states.
- Key-discovery caching and cache invalidation are delegated to the signer implementation; the kernel does not cache keys itself.

## Exact test results

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `make test` (CI subset) | 25/25 passed |
| Full pytest suite | **586 passed, 0 failed** (was 584+2 failed), 4 skipped |
| Drift gate | 16/16 passed |
| Independence tests | 23/23 passed |
| Idempotency tests | 5 passed, 2 skipped (reconciliation reserved) |

The 2 previously-failing tests (`test_2_same_operation_same_action_returns_prior_outcome` and `test_3_same_operation_different_action_conflicts`) now PASS.

title: Harden Kernel as reference execution-boundary verifier (Phase 4)
body:
## Summary

Hardens the Kernel as the reference execution-boundary verifier. The Kernel answers one question: *Does this proof authorise this exact action, against this exact target, with these exact parameters, at this boundary, under this configured trust policy, right now?*

It does NOT answer whether the commercial workflow was sensible. It does NOT depend on Cloud, Permit, hosted organisations, UI state, approval screens, or subscription plans.

## Verification pipeline before and after

### Before (Phase A merged)

The PCCBVerifier enforced a two-phase ordering:
- Phase A (pre-auth): structure, signature structure, canonicalisation, signature verification.
- Phase B (post-auth): time, audience, scope, intent_id, tenant, subject, **action**, **target**, action_hash.

**Issues:**
1. No protocol version check.
2. Field comparisons used `!=` (ad-hoc object equality), not canonical representations.
3. Action was checked before target (wrong order per the brief).
4. No boundary/resource binding.
5. No authority reference binding.
6. No revocation status check.
7. No verifier identity for receipt linkage.

### After (this PR)

The PCCBVerifier enforces an explicit **15-step pipeline**:

**Phase A (pre-auth, non-mutating):**
1. Input structure and size limits
2. **Supported protocol version** (NEW — contract name/version check)
3. Canonicalisation
4. Issuer and key resolution under configured trust policy
5. Signature verification

**Phase B (post-auth, non-mutating):**
6. Time validity
7. Audience binding (**canonical comparison** — CHANGED from `!=`)
8. **Resource or boundary binding** (NEW — optional `boundary_id`)
9. **Target binding** (canonical comparison — **MOVED BEFORE action**)
10. Action binding (canonical comparison — CHANGED from `!=`)
11. Exact parameter digest (action_hash)
12. **Authority reference binding** (NEW — documented, no-op for PCCBs without escrow_id)
13. **Revocation status** (NEW — optional `revocation_checker`, fail-closed)

**Deferred to ProtectedExecutor (stateful):**
14. Replay state (DEFERRED — formally justified: verifier is stateless, executor owns replay store)
15. Execution eligibility (DEFERRED — policy decision in executor)

Replay is never consumed before the proof passes all non-mutating validation (steps 1–13). The verifier is stateless; the executor is stateful. This separation is the formally justified reason for the split.

## Security fixes

| Fix | Details |
|---|---|
| **Canonical comparison** | All field comparisons (audience, tenant, subject, action, target) now use `canonicalize_bytes()` via `_canonical_equal()` instead of ad-hoc `!=`. Objects with `to_dict()` are coerced to dicts before canonicalisation. Floats are rejected (ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1). |
| **Protocol version check** | Step 2: PCCB contract name/version validated before any cryptographic work. |
| **Boundary binding** | Step 8: optional `boundary_id` on the verifier — the PCCB's audience must match the configured boundary. |
| **Revocation checking** | Step 13: optional `revocation_checker` callable, called AFTER all other checks pass. Fail-closed on error. |
| **Target before action** | Steps 9→10 reordered per the brief's required ordering. Target mismatch is now caught before action mismatch. |
| **Verifier identity** | New `verifier_identity` field on PCCBVerifier for receipt linkage. |

## Proof fields enforced

| Field | Step | Comparison method |
|---|---|---|
| Contract name/version | 2 | String equality |
| Signature structure | 1 | Field presence + encoding check |
| Canonicalisation | 3 | `canonicalize_bytes()` (size + depth limits) |
| Signature | 5 | Cryptographic verification via signer |
| not_before / expires_at | 6 | Timestamp comparison with clock skew |
| Audience | 7 | **Canonical byte comparison** |
| Boundary | 8 | String equality (optional) |
| Target | 9 | **Canonical byte comparison** |
| Scope mode + capability | 10 | String + set membership |
| Intent ID | 10 | String equality |
| Tenant | 10 | **Canonical byte comparison** |
| Subject | 10 | **Canonical byte comparison** |
| Action | 10 | **Canonical byte comparison** |
| Parameter digest | 11 | SHA-256 hash recomputation |
| Authority reference | 12 | Documented (no-op without escrow_id) |
| Revocation | 13 | Optional callable (fail-closed) |

## Refusal disclosure behaviour

| Mode | Pre-auth failure | Post-auth failure |
|---|---|---|
| `public_generic` | `PROOF_INVALID` | `PROOF_INVALID` |
| `trusted_detailed` | `PROOF_INVALID` | Detailed code (e.g. `AUDIENCE_MISMATCH`) |
| `local_debug` | Granular code | Granular code |

Public callers never receive `SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `AUDIENCE_MISMATCH`, `TARGET_MISMATCH`, `ACTION_MISMATCH`, or `PARAMETER_MISMATCH` — all collapse to `PROOF_INVALID` under `public_generic`. This prevents oracle probing.

New refusal codes: `UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION` (step 2), `AUTHORITY_REVOKED` (step 13).

## Compatibility impact

| Change | Breaking? | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Target checked before action (steps 9→10) | **Refusal code change** — `TARGET_MISMATCH` returned instead of `INTENT_MISMATCH`/`ACTION_MISMATCH` when both differ | Updated 6 test files to accept `TARGET_MISMATCH` |
| Canonical comparison replaces `!=` | **No** — canonical comparison is stricter but produces the same result for correctly-constructed objects | None needed |
| New CorrelationRef fields | **No** — all optional with defaults | None needed |
| New PCCBVerifier fields | **No** — all optional with defaults | None needed |
| New refusal codes | **No** — additive | None needed |

## Independent issuer test result

All 23 independence tests pass:
1. ✅ Verify proof from Permit-like issuer (different key)
2. ✅ Verify proof from third-party issuer (not Actenon)
3. ✅ Verify resource-owner self-issued proof
4. ✅ Refuse tampered signature
5. ✅ Refuse missing signature
6. ✅ Refuse Cloud-looking payload with wrong audience
7. ✅ Run without Cloud installed (sys.modules + AST scan)
8. ✅ Run without Permit installed (sys.modules + AST scan)
9. ✅ Resource-owner-configured trusted issuer
10. ✅ Resource-owner rejects untrusted issuer
11. ✅ Resource-owner revocation checker (fail-closed)
12. ✅ Resource-owner boundary_id
13. ✅ public_generic hides signature failure
14. ✅ trusted_detailed discloses audience mismatch
15. ✅ public_generic hides audience mismatch
16. ✅ Canonical comparison (same/different/floats)
17. ✅ CorrelationRef linkage fields round-trip
18. ✅ Receipt proves what boundary verified

## Complete test results

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `make test` (CI subset) | **25/25 passed** |
| Full pytest suite | **584 passed, 2 pre-existing failures (audit K-04), 4 skipped** |
| Drift gate | **16/16 passed** |
| Independence tests (new) | **23/23 passed** |
| Conformance suite | **51/51 passed** (Actenon Verified, Conformance 1.0.0) |

The 2 pre-existing failures (`tests/security/test_operation_idempotency.py`) are from audit finding K-04 (replay vs idempotency conflation) — NOT caused by this change.

## Receipt/refusal integrity

Receipts now include (via CorrelationRef):
- `pccb_id` — proof identifier
- `action_hash` — action + parameter digest
- `request_id` — execution attempt identifier
- `execution_attempt_id` (NEW) — dedicated attempt ID
- `protocol_version` (NEW) — protocol version used
- `execution_mode` (NEW) — brokered or resource_owned
- `verifier_identity` (NEW) — which verifier checked this
- `target_digest` (NEW) — canonical target reference

The receipt proves **what the boundary verified and enforced** — not that the authority should have been issued.

title: Phase A — Integrate actenon-protocol v1.0.0 (refusal taxonomy + canonicalisation)
body:
## Summary

Integrates the pinned `actenon-protocol v1.0.0` contract into `actenon-kernel`. This is **Phase A** of the four-phase integration plan documented in [actenon-protocol/INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md](https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-protocol/blob/main/INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md#phase-a--kernel-highest-leverage-lowest-risk).

The goal is to eliminate hand-maintained semantic duplication between the kernel and the protocol without collapsing runtime boundaries. The kernel's refusal taxonomy and canonicalisation profile constants are now sourced from the pinned protocol package; no public API is removed.

## Pinned dependency

```toml
# pyproject.toml
dependencies = [
  "actenon-protocol @ git+https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-protocol.git@v1.0.0",
  "pyyaml>=6.0,<7",
]
```

The pin is to the `v1.0.0` tag (which points at commit `9bf491d` on `Actenon/actenon-protocol`). This is NOT an unbounded `latest` dependency — bumping the pin is an explicit, reviewable change.

## Changes

### `actenon/outcomes.py` — refusal taxonomy sourced from protocol

- `FailureCode` is now a direct alias for `actenon_protocol.RefusalCode` (the protocol's 20-code enum). Python StrEnum cannot be subclassed once it has members, so `FailureCode = RefusalCode` (identity, not subclass).
- `TAXONOMY_VERSION` is sourced from the protocol.
- The 11 historical kernel-specific names (`PCCB_REQUIRED`, `PCCB_EXPIRED`, `DUPLICATE_REPLAY`, `NOT_ACTIVE`, `REVOKED`, `EXPIRED`, `SCOPE_DENIED`, `OUT_OF_SCOPE`, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `ENGINE_ERROR`) are preserved as module-level alias constants that resolve to the canonical protocol codes via the protocol's `compatibility_aliases` map.
- `refusal_code_to_failure_code()` now resolves via `actenon_protocol.resolve_alias()` first, then falls back to the historical `_REFUSAL_CODE_MAP`. Unknown codes raise `KeyError` — they are NOT silently mapped to a generic outcome (per the integration brief: "Do not silently map unknown failures to success or to a misleading generic outcome").
- New helpers `to_disclosed_code()`, `to_internal_code()`, `to_retryable()` re-export the protocol's disclosure-policy functions for kernel consumers.

### `actenon/proof/canonical.py` — canonicalisation profile sourced from protocol

- `CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE`, `LEGACY_CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE`, `ACCEPTED_CANONICALIZATION_PROFILES`, and `CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE_VERSION` are now sourced from `actenon_protocol`.
- The kernel's US-spelling attribute names (`canonicalization`) are preserved for backward compatibility; the values are identical to the protocol's British-spelling constants (`canonicalisation`).

### `tests/test_protocol_drift.py` — 16-test drift gate

Covers:
1. Protocol version is pinned to `1.0.0`.
2. Taxonomy versions agree between kernel and protocol.
3. `FailureCode` IS `RefusalCode` (identity, not subclass).
4. Historical aliases (`PCCB_REQUIRED`, etc.) resolve to canonical codes via both the protocol's `resolve_alias()` and the kernel's `refusal_code_to_failure_code()`.
5. Unknown refusal codes raise `KeyError` (not silently mapped).
6. Every code the kernel's verifier emits is registered in the protocol catalogue.
7. Canonicalisation profile label agrees.
8. Legacy canonicalisation profile agrees.
9. Accepted canonicalisation profiles agree.
10. The rejected label `actenon-jcs-sha256-v1` is not accepted.
11. Kernel and protocol produce byte-identical canonicalisation for shared test inputs.
12. Floats are rejected by both kernel (`TypeError`) and protocol (`CanonicalisationError`).
13. Identifier-prefix regex agrees.
14. Kernel does not import Cloud or Permit.
15. Protocol does not import Kernel.
16. Unsupported major protocol versions are rejected by the pydantic type.

### `tests/integration/test_installed_console_script.py` — install protocol from GitHub

The test creates a fresh venv and `pip install`s the kernel. With the new `actenon-protocol` dependency, the install step must first fetch the protocol from `git+https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-protocol.git@v1.0.0` (the protocol is not yet on PyPI; this is the same pattern the kernel already uses for its own dependencies).

### `.github/workflows/protocol-drift.yml` — CI drift gate

Runs on push, PR, and nightly. Fails when:
- The drift gate test fails.
- The protocol version pin in `pyproject.toml` is missing or wrong.
- An unregistered refusal code is emitted by kernel code.
- Canonicalisation byte output diverges between kernel and protocol.

## Boundary preservation

Verified by `tests/test_protocol_drift.py::test_kernel_does_not_import_cloud_or_permit` and `test_protocol_does_not_import_kernel`:

- Kernel does not import `actenon_cloud` or `actenon_permit`. ✓
- Protocol does not import `actenon` (kernel). ✓

## Compatibility

| Surface | Before | After | Breaking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FailureCode.PCCB_REQUIRED` | enum member | module-level alias constant resolving to `PROOF_MISSING` | No — code that does `FailureCode.PCCB_REQUIRED` continues to work, but the value is now `FailureCode.PROOF_MISSING` |
| `FailureCode.SIGNATURE_INVALID` | enum member | enum member (same name in protocol) | No |
| `refusal_code_to_failure_code("PCCB_REQUIRED")` | returns `FailureCode.PCCB_REQUIRED` | returns `FailureCode.PROOF_MISSING` (canonical) | **Behaviour change** — callers comparing to `FailureCode.PCCB_REQUIRED` will see `FailureCode.PROOF_MISSING` instead. Both compare equal because `PCCB_REQUIRED` is an alias for `PROOF_MISSING` with the same underlying value. |
| `CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE` | `"ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1"` (literal) | `"ACTENON-JCS-STRICT-1"` (sourced from protocol) | No — same string value |
| `TAXONOMY_VERSION` | `"1"` (literal) | `"1"` (sourced from protocol) | No |

## Test results

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_protocol_drift.py` (new) | **16/16 passed** |
| `make test` (CI subset) | **25/25 passed** |
| Full pytest (`actenon` + `tests`) | **561 passed, 2 failed, 4 skipped** |
| `tests/integration/test_installed_console_script.py` | **passed** (was failing before the protocol dep was added to the install step) |

The 2 failures (`tests/security/test_operation_idempotency.py`) are **pre-existing** — they were identified in the programme-level audit (finding K-04) and are NOT caused by this integration. They document the kernel's known replay-vs-idempotency conflation, which is out of scope for this phase.

## Duplicate definitions removed

| Duplicated definition | Was in | Now sourced from |
|---|---|---|
| `FailureCode` enum (16 members) | `actenon/outcomes.py` | `actenon_protocol.RefusalCode` (20 members; 16 historical names preserved as aliases) |
| `TAXONOMY_VERSION = "1"` | `actenon/outcomes.py` (literal) | `actenon_protocol.TAXONOMY_VERSION` |
| `CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE` | `actenon/proof/canonical.py` (literal) | `actenon_protocol.CANONICALISATION_PROFILE` |
| `LEGACY_CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE` | `actenon/proof/canonical.py` (literal) | `actenon_protocol.LEGACY_CANONICALISATION_PROFILE` |
| `ACCEPTED_CANONICALIZATION_PROFILES` | `actenon/proof/canonical.py` (frozenset literal) | `actenon_protocol.ACCEPTED_CANONICALISATION_PROFILES` |
| `CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE_VERSION` | `actenon/proof/canonical.py` (literal) | `actenon_protocol.CANONICALISATION_PROFILE_VERSION` |

## Aliases retained

All 16 existing `FailureCode` enum member names are retained as resolvable aliases:
`PCCB_REQUIRED`, `PCCB_EXPIRED`, `DUPLICATE_REPLAY`, `SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `ACTION_MISMATCH`, `AUDIENCE_MISMATCH`, `NOT_ACTIVE`, `REVOKED`, `EXPIRED`, `SCOPE_DENIED`, `OUT_OF_SCOPE`, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `ENGINE_ERROR` — plus the 4 protocol-only codes (`PROOF_MISSING`, `PROOF_EXPIRED`, `REPLAY_DETECTED`, `AUTHORITY_REVOKED`, `POLICY_REFUSAL`, etc.) now accessible directly.

## Breaking changes

**None for public API.** The only behaviour change is that `refusal_code_to_failure_code("PCCB_REQUIRED")` now returns `FailureCode.PROOF_MISSING` (canonical) instead of `FailureCode.PCCB_REQUIRED` (historical). These two values compare equal because they are the same underlying enum member. Existing code that does `if fc == FailureCode.PCCB_REQUIRED:` continues to work; existing code that does `if fc.value == "PCCB_REQUIRED":` will now see `"PROOF_MISSING"` and needs to migrate to `if fc == FailureCode.PCCB_REQUIRED:` or `if fc.value == "PROOF_MISSING":`.

## Drift gates added

1. `tests/test_protocol_drift.py` — 16 tests (runs in CI and locally).
2. `.github/workflows/protocol-drift.yml` — CI workflow (push, PR, nightly).
3. The CI workflow also scans kernel source for unregistered refusal-code strings.

## After merge

- Phase B (Permit) can begin: Permit already imports `FailureCode` from the kernel, so it transitively gets the protocol-sourced taxonomy.
- Phase C (Cloud) can begin: Cloud's `SIGNATURE_INVALID` vs `PROOF_INVALID` test drift (audit finding C-01) can be resolved by asserting on `disclosed_code` from the protocol.
- Phase D (Scan) is independent.

body:
## Phase 2A — Verifier Oracle-Hardening Design and Regression Tests

### Security objective
Unauthenticated or invalidly-signed forged proofs must not use detailed public refusal codes as a field-by-field semantic oracle.

### What changed
- 11 regression tests defining the verifier hardening requirement (8 expected to FAIL until Phase 2B; 3 verify preserved post-authentication semantics)
- Design note documenting the 3-mode refusal-disclosure policy (public_generic / trusted_detailed / local_debug) and the implementation plan

### No production code changed
This commit adds tests and a design note only. The verifier implementation is unchanged. The 8 failing tests define the target behaviour for Phase 2B.

### Test results
- 3 passing: tests 6-8 (validly-signed post-authentication mismatches preserve detailed codes)
- 8 failing: tests 1-5, 9-11 (forged proofs must return PROOF_INVALID; local_debug mode; receipt redaction; env guard) — all expected to fail until Phase 2B
